decisions.statement: The window swept by is the one the file property states rather than one here.
A property stating no window is reached by no sweep.
The page types swept are the ones declaring a property that states a window.
A page type declares such a property through what that page type extends too.
A property a file property group carries is swept under the group's slug and then its own.
Which pages a page type has is what the index answers rather than a folder listed.
A record file's path is composed out of its page's path and its section.
A stream is there where the file that path names is there.
A stream whose first part is gone is found by the part beside it.
Nothing here reads the path of every file the repository holds.
A line is judged by the instant that line states it ran at.
A line stating no instant this can read is kept.
A line that will not read as json is kept.
The lines left are written again from the first part up.
A part is filled by counting each line's bytes rather than weighing the part again.
A part left holding nothing goes rather than being left empty.
The first part goes too where the window leaves no line at all.
A writer appends to the highest part there is, and makes the first part again where none is.
A stream is swept under the turn its writer takes over that stream's first part.
A stream is left as that stream is where a part of it is absent or will not read.
A stream whose first part alone is gone is swept by nothing while its writer still appends.
Nothing is taken away unless the sweep is asked to.
A stream whose turn does not come is left as that stream is and counted.
A sweep takes a turn between streams, which is what lets it hear a stop.
A sweep told to stop finishes the stream it holds and reaches no further one.
A sweep told to stop says which stream it got to and refuses.
The refusal is an exit code the unit does not count as success.

definition: every line beside a page past the window its property states taken away
